'''Heinrich Friedrich Gretschel''' (21 October 1830, in Prietitz near Elstra, [[Germany]] – 2 February 1892, in [[Freiburg, Switzerland]]) was a German [[mathematician]] and scientist.

In 1847, Gretschel became a student at the Technischen Bildungsanstalt (now [[TU Dresden]]). On 28 April 1851 he was enrolled at [[Leipzig University]], where he studied mathematics, natural sciences and ancient languages. In 1854, he passed the examination for the higher school office in the first ranking and became a teacher at the Leipziger Gesamtgymnasium.<ref name="Freiberg">{{cite web|title=Heinrich Friedrich Gretschel (1830–1892) Mathematiker und Universalgelehrter|url=http://tu-freiberg.de/sites/default/files/media/fakultaet-fuer-mathematik-und-informatik-fakultaet-1-9277/poster/gretschel.pdf|website=TU Bergakademie Freiberg|accessdate=6 July 2017}}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

On 2 January 1873 he was promoted by the Faculty of Philosophy of the University of Leipzig as a result of completing the mathematical dissertation, ''Lehrbuch zur Einführung in die organische Geometrie'' ("Introduction to organic geometry").<ref>Universitätsarchiv Leipzig, Personalakten, Promotionen 1810–1969, Signatur: Phil. Fak. B 128 b</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Heinrich Friedrich Gretschel|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=213244|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project|accessdate=6 July 2017}}</ref><ref name="Freiberg"/>

On 7 January 1873 he became professor of mathematics and geometric construction at the [[Bergakademie Freiberg]], a position that he held until his death in 1892.<ref name="Freiberg"/> 
In 1876, Gretschel became a Bergrat professor.<ref name="Freiberg"/> During 1875–1880, 1881–1883, and 1886–1889 he belonged to the Bergakademischen Senate.<ref>{{cite web|title=Senat (bis 1945)|url=http://tu-freiberg.de/ze/archiv/geschichte/senat-1945|website=TU Bergakademie Freiberg|accessdate=6 July 2017}}</ref>

Gretschel wrote and lectured in a wide range of fields, publishing books about [[meteorology]], [[physics]], [[chemistry]], [[astronomy]], [[geometry]] and [[cartography]].<ref name="Freiberg"/> He and [[Georg Bornemann]] wrote about the organization of the [[periodic table]], published as ''Das Naturliche System der Elemente'' (1883).<ref>{{Cite book | title = Graphic Representations of the Periodic System during One Hundred Years | publisher = [[University of Alabama Press]] | year = 1974 | pages = 251 | isbn = 0-8173-3200-6 }}</ref><ref name="Elemente">{{cite book|last1=Gretschel|first1=Heinrich Friedrich|last2=Bornemann|first2=Georg|title=Das Naturliche System der Elemente. Jahrbuch der Erfindungen|date=1883|publisher=241–306|location=Leipzig|pages=241–306|edition=I9ten Jahrgang}}</ref>
Gretschel also wrote about the construction of stringed instruments in the [[violin]] family<ref name="Katz">{{cite book|last1=Katz|first1=Mark|title=The violin : a research and information guide|date=2006|publisher=Routledge|location=New York|isbn=9780815336372|page=44|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ScAPGsv8W5gC&pg=PA44|accessdate=6 July 2017}}</ref> and co-wrote a book on the construction of the [[pianoforte]] with [[Julius Blüthner]], ''Lehrbuch des Pianofortebaues'' (1872).<ref name="Steiner">{{cite book|last1=Steiner|first1=Thomas|title=Instruments à claviers – expressivité et flexibilité sonore : actes des Rencontres Internationales Harmoniques, Lausanne 2002; [Rencontre Internationale de Musiciens, Musicologues, Facteurs d'Instruments de Musique, Restaurateurs et Conservateurs de Musée] = Keyboard instruments – flexibility of sound and expression : proceedings of the Harmoniques International Congress, Lausanne 2002|date=2004|publisher=Lang|location=Bern [u.a.]|isbn=9783039102440|page=182|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YPw9zLNEutIC&pg=PA182|accessdate=6 July 2017}}</ref>
